headline: High: shared-file and API-backed RAG workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; Authelia’s broad egress can amplify compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts, so attacker-controlled content can become model input. Authelia can sit in front of web apps via ForwardAuth/OIDC, creating a plausible bridge if its outputs or protected pages are fed into Kotaemon. No direct shared channel is documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Authelia-protected pages or auth responses are copied into Kotaemon ingestion sources, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF the operator connects both agents through a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge, untrusted text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Restrict Kotaemon ingestion to trusted sources only.
Strip scripts and hidden text before indexing.
Use a separate workspace for Authelia logs and exports.
Add a human review step before any prompt-fed document is indexed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all ingested content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and stores files under ./ktem_app_data, while Authelia has broad network egress and handles OAuth/OIDC flows. If both touch the same workspace or secrets are copied into documents, leakage can occur in default RAG-style operation. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or mounted volume, Kotaemon may ingest Authelia artifacts.
IF API keys or auth logs are placed into Kotaemon sources, they can be surfaced in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Keep Authelia logs out of Kotaemon ingestion paths.
Store secrets in a separate vault, not in documents.
Disable indexing of config and env files.
Review the first 20 retrieved chunks for secret leakage.
requires-engineering: enforce per-source allowlists and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls for OIDC/ForwardAuth, and Kotaemon can call multiple LLM and document APIs while supporting multiple instances. Their write surfaces are different, but overlapping networked side effects can still conflict if they share credentials or upstream services. Lack of explicit locking or shared-resource details keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF both agents use the same upstream API key or OAuth principal, requests can race or overwrite shared quotas.
IF both are deployed against the same external service, one agent's retries can interfere with the other's rate limits.
mitigations: Use separate API keys per agent.
Set per-agent rate limits.
Rotate credentials so each agent has distinct scopes.
Monitor 429/5xx spikes during parallel runs.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can render retrieved content and citations, so it may treat upstream text as authoritative. Authelia’s auth-related outputs can become inputs to that pipeline if the operator feeds them in. Because no direct automation from Kotaemon to external actions is documented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Authelia-generated text is pasted into Kotaemon as source material, Kotaemon may propagate errors or false claims.
IF Kotaemon answers are used as operational guidance without verification, downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require source verification before acting on Kotaemon outputs.
Mark auth-related text as untrusted in the workflow.
Compare retrieved citations against original sources.
Limit Kotaemon to read-only advisory use for auth topics.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon touches API keys, chat transcripts, and document corpora, while Authelia performs authentication and broad egress. If regulated identity or transcript data flows through Kotaemon’s external model APIs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so I cannot justify high.
conditions: IF regulated identity data or transcripts are indexed in Kotaemon, external API retention policies become relevant.
IF Authelia logs are forwarded into Kotaemon, subject-access and deletion workflows may diverge.
mitigations: Exclude regulated records from Kotaemon indexes.
Confirm vendor retention settings for each API provider.
Separate auth logs from support corpora.
Document deletion/export handling for both systems.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement.
